# Safety Matrix (Machine-Read Table)

This is the full table behind [doc/spec/safety_model.md](../../doc/spec/safety_model.md), which gives each row as a short readable entry. The table is read by `scripts/check_safety_model.sh` and `scripts/check_route_coverage.sh`: every row names the probes that prove it, the compiler constructs ("routes") its mechanism depends on, and an evidence level. `check_safety_model.sh` also fails when an entry on the readable page differs from its row here.

Columns: Property, Claim, Mechanism, Level and file, Boundary, Side (`safe` or `unsafe`), Proven by (links to probes and tests), Routes, Evidence (`example`, `routes`, `fuzzed` or `argued`).

| **Type Size Fits**                                                         | A type whose size exceeds `isize::MAX` is a compile error, so a size never wraps and an in-bounds element address cannot leave the signed 64-bit range                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `type_size` multiplies and adds with a checked result (`TYPE_SIZE_OVERFLOW`, above `TYPE_SIZE_LIMIT` = `isize::MAX`; `TYPE_SIZE_TOO_DEEP`, past the 100-level depth limit), through nested arrays, struct field offsets with alignment, enum payloads, tuples and the depth limit; a type that computes to one is rejected where the program writes the type (`check_type_size` in the resolver), so `sizeof`, a field type, a `Vec` element type and an alias all report; a declaration with no type parameters is laid out and checked even when nothing names it (`check_declared_type_size` in the driver) `src/driver/module.zrl` `check_declared_type_size`)                                                                            | Every type expression is checked; every non-generic declaration is laid out once even if unused, and a generic declaration at each instance. The limit leaves a type of at most `isize::MAX` bytes, which the backend may still refuse to materialise in a stack frame (no stack probe, `doc/SAFETY.md` §3) A store of a reference into storage owned by this frame (a collection, a box or an arena) through a pointer or reference parameter (`*out = ...`), a struct field (`h.s = ...`), a tuple field (`out.1 = ...`), via a collection method call (`out.push(...)`), through a callee function, method, helper, or trait method, or into a `&mut` destination derived from a parameter by a callee or method call is rejected (`cannot store ... a reference into storage owned by this frame (a collection, a box or an arena) cannot outlive the frame`; `check_assign` and `check_call_stores_escapes` in `src/check_zir.zrl`, probes 336-340, 344-347, 351-355, 359-364; accepted twins: moving a whole collection, viewing a parameter's arena, copying an element, storing a static string, or storing into a local destination, probes 341-343, 348-350, 356-358, 365-367). A view of a closure's owned capture counts as storage owned by this frame under the store rule: storing it through a captured `&mut`, into another capture, or into a global is rejected (probes 368-374; accepted twins: probes 375-377). A by-value aggregate that a call returned carries the pointer the call was given, and a reference to a local aggregate that reaches the callee through a value (a load of a slot, an identity call, a phi) is read as pointing at stack where its slot is unknown (the summary pass's `returns_via`/`stashes_via` bits and `arg_contents`; probes 391-399 and 400-404, accepted twins 399 and 405); A direct call whose callee writes a parameter's storage into another parameter or a global is rejected at the call (`check_call_stores_stack`); a `fn` value is called where no check can see the arguments, so a function or closure with that contract cannot become one (`FuncAddr` is refused: ``region escape: the function stores a reference into memory that outlives a call through a `fn` value``, `check_fn_value` in `src/verify.zrl`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | ZIL Verifier (`src/verify.zrl`, `note_stack_ptr_written`, `check_call_stores_stack`, `check_fn_value`); ZIR Borrow Checker (`src/check_zir.zrl`, `check_assign`, `check_call_stores_escapes`)                  | Intraprocedural for a direct store. | **Region Escape: Through a Call** (§11.2.4)                                | A stack pointer passed to a function cannot come back out of the frame through it: not handed back (`return stash(&mut s)` dangles like `return &mut s`), and not stored by the callee into memory that outlives the frame (`put(h, &x)` with `fn put(h: &mut H, p: &i32) { h.r = p; }`, or into a global)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Each function's body is summarized by which parameters' own storage its result may point into and which it writes outside its frame, into which parameters' memory (`ret_storage`, `stores_storage`, `store_targets`), iterated to a fixpoint over the call graph and written to `.zri`. At a call, a result tied to a stack argument points to the stack; a stack argument the callee stores away is a write of a stack pointer to each target, an error unless the target is in this frame too. A slice argument counts by where it points, not where its header is | **Region Escape: Reference Returned Through a Call** (§11.2.4)             | A reference into a local's own storage, obtained through a call (`let c = C {..}; return c.get();`), is not returned, whether as `&T`, `Option<&T>` or a struct or slice holding it; nor a reference into a local array obtained through a slice argument (`first(&a)`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Each function's body says which parameters' own storage its result may point into (`ret_storage`: an address derived from the parameter by field/index steps, with no load through it). A call's result tied that way to a stack argument points to the stack, or, arriving in the return slot, makes the slot hold a stack pointer; the existing return and store checks then reject it. Written to `.zri` (`#[summary(.., storage = ..)]`) so importers see it. `v.as_slice()` / `v.get(i)` on a local Vec point into the buffer, loaded through `self`: a return rejects a borrow the returned value holds whose root is a local whose type owns storage (`Vec`, `String`, `ByteVec`, `HashMap`, `Box`, `Arena`, or anything containing one recursively) unless the local's provenance proves the storage outlives the frame - a parameter (or a value copied from one), a `*_raw` constructor, or any other `unsafe fn`, whose caller took the obligation, or a constructor anchored to an `&Arena` argument that is itself external (`buffer_external` / `buffer_anchored` in `src/driver/module.zrl`; `type_owns_storage` / `local_storage_external` in `src/check_zir.zrl`). Default-deny: unknown provenance answers "this frame owns it" (probes 278-292, 336-343, `String::as_slice` and `split` into a local arena included; a returned or stored view of a local collection is rejected whether or not the collection frees its buffer). Moving a field that needs dropping out of a value (`let x = w.d;`) is rejected, since partial moves are not tracked per field; so is `[v; n]` with n > 1 for such a `v` | Each local whose type needs dropping (own `drop` function, or owns one by value) gets a runtime drop flag: false where it is declared, set when initialised or reassigned, cleared when moved; scope exit and reassignment drop only while it is set. `ZirStmt.Drop`/`DropIfLive` lower to drop glue that recurses through fields, the active enum payload, tuple elements and array elements; pointers are never followed. | **Pointer Forgery (Raw Pointers)**                                         | A pointer forged from an integer is unchecked _when it is used_: the dereference or the conversion to a reference is what is gated (each on the pointer's own type), while the creation itself is safe                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `n as *T`, `@ptr_from_int<*T>` and `@ptr_cast<*T>` are safe: every use of a raw pointer is gated on its type, so gating the creation would add a marker and buy nothing, and a fixed address needs a spelling in a `static` (`ptr_forge_needs_unsafe`, `check_ptr_forge_is_marked` for the reference and slice results of the same intrinsics; `check_raw_deref_is_marked` for the use). Inside `unsafe`, the pointer is a direct address calculation and a bad dereference faults with SIGSEGV (139). The target of `=` and of a compound assignment must be a place (`check_assignment_target`): a literal, a computed value, a call result or a cast is refused before it can be treated as an address, so a computed integer cannot become a store address in checked code | **Stdlib `unsafe` Interiors**                                              | Every `unsafe` block in `stdlib/` trusts an invariant the type system does not check - a length that matches its allocation, an index that fits, a pointer that is live, arithmetic that cannot wrap - and checked code must not be able to break one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Each block states its invariant in a `// SAFETY:` comment, enforced in `make test` by `scripts/check_safety_comments.sh` (114 blocks in 16 of the 22 stdlib modules); the invariants checked code could otherwise break are closed: `Vec`/`ByteVec`/`HashMap`/`String`/`InternTable` fields are private behind narrow accessors (`cap`, `as_ptr`, `as_mut_ptr`, `raw_arena`, `unsafe fn set_len` that traps above `cap`, `HashMap::entry_at` that checks its index), every allocation size goes through `mem::size_of_n`/`grow_cap` (trap instead of wrap), `zoril_allocator_alloc`/`zoril_allocator_realloc` compare by subtracting from `capacity`, `str_sub` clamps with `len > s.len - start`, and `Args::get` compares its index in `usize` rather than `index as i32`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `stdlib/` (21 modules), `scripts/check_safety_comments.sh`, `stdlib/mem.zrl`                                                                                                                                   | The comments are a review artifact, not a proof: they say which invariant a block relies on, and only the five audited fault classes have tests. | **Encapsulation (Private Methods)** (§11.1.1, §11.1.2)                     | A method, associated function or associated constant that is not `pub` is nameable only from the module that declares its `impl`, so another module cannot reach a private invariant keeper (`c.bump()`, `Widget.SECRET`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `check_method_visible`/`check_private_visible` (`src/lower_zir/expr.zrl`) compare the impl's module with the module being lowered on every route to a member: a call on a receiver, a path call (`T.f(..)`, `T::f(..)`), a method taken as a value, and an associated constant. An impl of a trait is public, as the trait is, so its methods need no `pub`; a private field is rejected (`check_field_visible`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | ZIR Lowerer (method, associated-function and associated-constant resolution)                                                                                                                                   | Methods are checked across modules, so a program cannot call another module's private helper. The stdlib's private methods (`HashMap::alloc_in`, `String::write`, `Sha256::compress`) cannot break an invariant from checked code, so the rule enforces encapsulation rather than closing a hole; `unsafe` code stays outside the boundary by design | **Region Escape: Borrowed Value Dropped at Block End** (§7.2)              | A value leaving scope while something that outlives that scope still borrows it is rejected ("cannot let 'x' go out of scope while it is still borrowed"), not only when a reference escapes the function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `check_scope_end_borrowed` runs at every `ZirStmt.EndBorrow`; lowering emits that marker for each local whose scope exits, `borrow_counts` supplies the live-borrower test, and `borrowed_storage_is_local` skips storage behind a pointer, reference or slice deref (a `Box` deref counts, since the local's `Drop` frees it). Whether a borrow inherited through a call is the argument's own storage or only what it references is the borrow's recorded direct provenance (`ActiveBorrow.direct`), not a guess from types. Mutations: M90, M133                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | ZIR Borrow Checker (`src/check_zir.zrl`), ZIR Lowering (`src/lower_zir/decl.zrl`)                                                                                                                              | At every block boundary, not only at a block's own exit path; whether a borrow passed through a function call counts is decided by the storage summary - the mask each body's canonical ZIR gives (`compute_ret_storage_zir` in `src/check_zir.zrl`, run by `run_body_passes` before the borrow checker), the `.zri` one for an import, with `Drop` only as the fallback for a callee that has neither. A call inside a body uses its callee's mask once that is known, so a wrapper, a chain and a forwarding method read as the function that finally hands the address back. A callee whose mask is not known yet - a cycle (mutual recursion), or a body not yet read - makes the caller's mask unknown too: the function's masks are recorded as unknown, and a call to it is read as handing back each tied argument's own storage - the strict side, which `check_scope_end_borrowed` applies without the `Drop` exemption (probes [`167`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/167_recursion_cycle_storage_unknown.zrl), [`168`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/168_recursion_cycle_wrapper_storage_unknown.zrl), [`tests/error_reporting/err_block_scope_borrow_recursion_cycle.zrl`](../../tests/error_reporting/err_block_scope_borrow_recursion_cycle.zrl), [`err_block_scope_borrow_recursion_cycle_wrapper.zrl`](../../tests/error_reporting/err_block_scope_borrow_recursion_cycle_wrapper.zrl), [`err_block_scope_borrow_recursion_cycle_memo.zrl`](../../tests/error_reporting/err_block_scope_borrow_recursion_cycle_memo.zrl)). A callee the driver cannot resolve from the AST is not read as handing back _nothing_: a method whose receiver is a parameter is resolved by its declared type, and a call that stays unresolvable (a call through a function value or a function-pointer parameter, a variant constructor) is read as the worst case - the result may point into every argument's own storage - so the borrow counts without the `Drop` exemption (probes [`169`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/169_param_receiver_method_storage_unknown.zrl), [`170`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/170_unresolvable_callee_storage_unknown.zrl)). A borrow a value _inherits_ from an operand or a call keeps that operand's own classification: a struct literal holding `&x` counts at `x`'s scope end while a field holding what a call derived is still exempt, and a call through a function value - no summary to consult - is read as own storage ([`171`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/171_call_through_value_own_storage.zrl), [`172`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/172_aggregate_keeps_borrow_flag.zrl)). A closure's environment is read the same way: the captures' borrows keep their own classification, so a closure that captured a reference to a local counts at that local's scope end (probe [`173`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/173_closure_capture_keeps_borrow_flag.zrl), [`tests/error_reporting/err_block_scope_borrow_closure_capture.zrl`](../../tests/error_reporting/err_block_scope_borrow_closure_capture.zrl)), while a borrow whose base is the environment's own temporary stays exempt - that storage lives in the enclosing frame, where the escape analysis bounds it (the `err_closure_escapes_*` tests) and where counting it rejected every by-value capture | safe | **Value Forged by Cast**                                                   | `as` cannot make a slice, array, tuple, struct, enum or box out of another type, nor add `mut` to a slice, nor make a `bool` or a `char` out of a number in checked code                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | A cast whose resolved target is one of those types is accepted only as the identity, or from a slice of the same element type that is mutable or the target is not (`[mut T] as [T]`). The check reads the resolved type, so an alias does not hide the target. A cast to `bool` from any other type is refused outside `unsafe`: `5 as bool` kept the 5, and every two-armed `match` on it reached `zoril_abort` (exit 1); `n != 0` is the spelling that always yields a bool. `unsafe` permits the cast for both `bool` and `char`, as the escape hatch (a forged `bool` still aborts at the first two-armed `match`, and `unicode::char_from_u32` needs the `char` cast after its own range check). A cast to `char` is refused outside `unsafe`, except from a `u8` (every byte is a scalar value, so `b as char` and `let c: char = b` agree; `tests/language/basic/test_char_from_byte.zrl`): a wider number can be a surrogate or above U+10FFFF, which `Str`'s UTF-8 invariant and every char match assume cannot happen, and `unicode::char_from_u32` is the checked conversion. The intrinsics that make a value of `T` from a number or a pointer (`@int_cast<T>`, `@ptr_cast<T>`, `@ptr_from_int<T>`) go through the same check, so `@int_cast<char>(0xd800)` and `@int_cast<bool>(5)` are refused, and so is a C function pointer (`@int_cast<extern "C" fn(..)>(4096)`, `@ptr_cast` and `@ptr_from_int` too: `as` refused it and the intrinsic route did not; probe 263). A raw pointer may become a C function pointer only inside `unsafe`, where non-null is the caller's obligation; an integer may never become one; a function pointer casts to its own type (compared with `types_match`, not type ids) but not to a different signature, even in `unsafe` (probes 273-277). A `u8` still stands for a `char` implicitly (every byte is a scalar value, and a char literal is a `u8`); a wider or signed number does not (`implicit_conv_ok`). Operator operands are an allowlist that fails closed (`check_numeric_operands`, `check_unary_numeric_operand`, `check_equality_operands`): arithmetic takes integers (and floats where the operator is defined), bitwise and shifts integers, relational comparison integers, floats or chars; equality takes two operands of one comparable type and never a reference against an integer; `+`/`-` on a raw pointer inside `unsafe` is the only escape hatch. Unit, references in arithmetic, slices, function values, boxes, tuples, arrays, structs and enums are rejected by name | Frontend (`check_cast_validity`, `check_numeric_operands`, ### Routes: what each row's evidence walks

The `Routes` column names the compiler constructs a row's mechanism is a function of, in the vocabulary `zoril --emit-zir-stats` prints: `rv:<ZirRvalue variant>`, `stmt:<ZirStmt variant>`, `term:<ZirTerminator variant>`, `cfg:join` (a block with two or more predecessors) and `cfg:backedge` (an edge to a block at or before its source). A row resolved before or after ZIR (parser, type checker, backend, runtime) lists `-`.

A cell may name only a route a **borrow** can travel through into a reported error: the carrying vocabulary `src/route_set.zrl` defines, which `--emit-zir-stats` prints on its `carry` line. That is the rvalues that create a borrow (`Ref`, `RefMut`) and the ones that put one into a value that can hold it - a copy (`Use`), a call or a call through a value (`Call`, `CallPtr`), an aggregate literal or a payload extraction (`StructLiteral`, `Tuple`, `Array`, `EnumVariant`, `EnumPayload`), a box or a repeated array (`Boxed`, `ArrayRepeat`), a cast whose target is not a raw pointer (`Cast`), and a closure's environment (`FuncAddr`) - plus the statements that bind, move or end a borrow (`Let`, `Assign`, `EndBorrow`) and the two CFG shapes. Everything else is excluded, each for a reason no probe can get around:

- every terminator (`term:Jmp`, `term:Branch`, `term:Ret`, `term:Unreachable`): a borrow conflict is reported at the statement or rvalue being checked, never at a jump;
- `rv:GetEnv`: the closure environment is a raw pointer, and no borrow is tracked through one (`type_holds_reference` refuses a raw pointer, so `inherit_rv_borrows` has no case for it); a capture's borrow reaches the closure through `rv:FuncAddr` instead;
- the rvalues whose result is a number (`Const`, `BinaryOp`, `UnaryOp`, `Sizeof`, `StringConst`, `VariantCheck`, `GlobalAddr`, `PtrFromInt`, `Syscall`, `Intrinsic`), which cannot hold a reference;
- `stmt:Drop`, `stmt:DropIfLive` and `stmt:Intrinsic`: a drop reports an ownership error, not a borrow conflict, so no rejection travels through one; the borrow end that is checked is the `EndBorrow` the lowering emits.

`scripts/check_route_coverage.sh` refuses a cell naming a route outside that vocabulary before it looks at coverage at all, and its `--selftest` plants such a cell (`term:Jmp`) so the refusal cannot quietly disappear. The gate also prints what it walked - how many rows list routes, how many routes, and how many cited `compile_reject` probes carried them - so an empty column cannot read like a full one.

A list is not evidence by itself. `zoril --emit-zir-stats` prints a `reject-via` line: the routes a reported rejection travelled through - the rvalue that created the borrow, every step that carried it, the statement or terminator that reported the error, and whether it crossed a join or a back-edge. `scripts/check_route_coverage.sh` compiles every probe the row cites and counts a route only when the probe declares `// expected: compile_reject`, the compiler rejects it, and its `reject-via` names the route. Accepted probes, `runtime_trap` probes, `known_gap` probes, runtime-fault probes and cited tests without a probe header are not evidence for a route. That population is the point: a hole is a program the compiler _accepts_, and a program the compiler refuses that merely contains the constructs (a construct census, not a route) proves nothing about any of them.

**Six rows are at `routes` today**: Borrow Aliasing (Exclusive Mutable) with 12 routes, Arena Use After Reset or Free with 15, Borrow Aliasing: Returned References, Region Escape: Borrowed Value Dropped at Block End and Closure Capture by Reference with 8 each, and Capturing Closure Escape with 5 - 56 route mentions in all, walked by 50 of the probes those rows cite. Two probes complete them: [`233_slice_cast_carries_borrow.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/233_slice_cast_carries_borrow.zrl), whose `[mut i32] as [i32]` cast carries the borrow (`rv:Cast`), and [`234_array_literal_carries_borrow.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/234_array_literal_carries_borrow.zrl), whose `[&mut z]` literal does the same (`rv:Array`); before them no rejection had travelled through either route.

The other 66 rows sit at `example` with `-`, for one of two measured reasons:

- **Their mechanism's error records no route.** Only a borrow conflict adds to `reject_via` (`report_borrow_conflict`). A region-escape error comes from the ZIL verifier, which has no ZIR route to record, and an ownership error (use after move, double drop, drop once, move out of a borrow, a linear leak) is reported by `report_place_error` / `report_var_error`, which record nothing. A row in those families could only list a route its own cited probes would not walk, so it stays at `example`.
- **Their cited probes are now refused earlier, by a different check.** The two region-escape rows that cite [`211_ret_storage_local_alias.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/211_ret_storage_local_alias.zrl), [`212_ret_storage_struct_wrap.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/212_ret_storage_struct_wrap.zrl) or [`220_same_type_borrow_loop_escape.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/220_same_type_borrow_loop_escape.zrl) get a borrow conflict at a scope end ("cannot let 'x' go out of scope while it is still borrowed") before the region-escape check ever runs, so those probes' reject-via describes the borrow mechanism, not the row's. Crediting the row with it would be the over-broad list this column exists to avoid; the probes that do fire the region-escape check ([`44_dangling_stack_slice_store.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/44_dangling_stack_slice_store.zrl) onwards) record no route.

The accepted [`232_reference_route_census.zrl`](../../bench/safety_matrix/probes/232_reference_route_census.zrl) remains a lowering smoke test - it must accept and lower at least one function - but its routes are not a row's evidence. A row is raised to `routes` by a probe whose rejection travels through every route it lists; the gate's `--selftest` pins the distinction with a program that contains `box` but fails on an unrelated use after move (it must fail naming `rv:Boxed`), with probe 206, whose rejection does travel through the box (it must pass), with a cell naming `term:Jmp` (it must be refused as a route a borrow cannot travel through), and with a cell listing `rv:Cast` beside a probe whose rejection never used one (it must fail until probe 233 is cited).

The matrix's "Proven by" examples and this route set answer different questions. The examples show that the mechanism fires on the shapes someone thought of; the route set shows that every shape the mechanism _branches on_ is among them. A hole is a route in the second sense: a construct the checker has a case for that no probe reaches.
